sources.location: Dense Azure industrial analytics and predictive-maintenance stress test
Seven Microsoft Azure architecture diagrams supplied by the user

facts.claim: The reference workload combines streaming equipment telemetry, operational records, and unstructured maintenance content.
Streaming and scheduled ingestion remain separate before converging in the analytical platform.
A lake, operational store, and SQL warehouse support different latency and serving needs.
The architecture includes stream processing, batch engineering, model training, and maintenance knowledge enrichment.
Real-time inference and analytical serving are separated into explicit nested groups.
Operations applications, BI dashboards, and alert automation consume different products of the platform.
Identity, secrets, observability, security posture, delivery, and policy apply across the workload.
The reference set uses weighted phase columns, nested execution groups, numbered handoffs, connector gutters, bypass rails, and a horizontal foundation band for dense lifecycle views.
Azure service nodes use official Microsoft architecture icons with the represented product name adjacent to the icon.

assumptions: The diagram is a logical reference architecture rather than a subscription, region, or network deployment topology.
Connected equipment, operational systems, and maintenance documents are generic external source categories, not Azure products.
The example intentionally includes both predictive ML and maintenance knowledge search to stress nested and parallel flows.
